claims.text: The rider's claim is narrow and specific: a $3.00 ERP charge for a gantry on a road the trip never used. The fare ledger itself concedes the point — the single ERP line, 'AYE Alexandra Rd gantry' at $3.00, is flagged on_optimal_route = false, and the optimal route's own ERP total is $0.00. The rider was billed for a gantry that is not on the route they booked.

The driver's own GPS trace never comes within 250 m of the charged gantry. The nearest fix to the AYE Alexandra Rd gantry is 330.73 m away, at 11:10:50, and the trace does not bracket the gantry's closest approach. Under POL-RD-09 a gantry is matched to the trace by treating any fix within 250 m as a crossing; 330.73 m is outside that radius, so the trace does not place the vehicle at this gantry.

This is a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4): a charge line for a gantry the gps_trace never passes is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists. The $3.00 line should be refunded in full and the case recorded as a billing-integrity finding.

The rider's claim does not depend on establishing a route deviation, and I do not overreach by asserting one. The trace measures 20.58 km against an optimal of 19.6 km — an excess of 0.98 km, or 5.00%, which fails both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km). The derived deviation status is 'no deviation'. The rider's remedy therefore rests on the ERP pass-through correction alone, not on POL-RD-02.

The driver's counter-statement — 'The ERP is charged by the system' — cites no evidence ID and identifies no gantry, road or route. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded. It does not discharge the driver's burden of showing the charge was properly incurred.

No traffic advisory covers this trip window: the advisory artifact is MISSING with weight 0.0, so no external traffic cause can be tested or credited. Under POL-RD-13 the driver's bare assertion of a system charge, unsupported by any advisory, carries no weight, and the absence of an advisory is itself citable.

The rider's profile does not bar this claim. The rider has 1 deviation claim in 60 days and 0 substantiated — well below the POL-RD-08 threshold of 4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated — so no additional corroboration beyond the trace is required. The trace here is clean: 100% coverage, 10 s sampling, no gaps, max gap 0 sec, so POL-RD-07 impairment does not arise.

The fare ledger is internally consistent and unimpaired: it reconciles to a total charged of $30.55, with the $3.00 ERP line itemised separately. The refund sought is the $3.00 pass-through correction, which is below the $8.00 execution threshold and is a standalone correction under POL-RD-09(4), not a POL-RD-02 recomputation.

claims.text: The rider's own claim is that an ERP charge of $3.00 was levied for a road the trip never used. The fare breakdown shows exactly one ERP line, the AYE Alexandra Rd gantry at $3.00, and the platform's own derived erp_gantry_proximity block records that this gantry is NOT on the optimal route (on_optimal_route = false) and that the closest the driver's trace ever came to it was 330.73 m, at fix index 128 (2026-08-30T11:10:50). Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge line for a gantry the gps_trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure and is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists. The 330.73 m nearest approach exceeds the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09 sets, so the gantry is unmatched and the $3.00 must be returned.

The distance-and-time side of the fare is not in dispute and should not be disturbed. The platform's own deviation computation on the trace records excess_km of 0.98 and excess_pct of 5.00 against the booked optimal of 19.6 km, and classifies the trip as 'no deviation'. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests therefore fail: 5.00% is far below the 20% threshold and 0.98 km is only just above the 0.8 km absolute threshold, so the conjunctive test is not met. No distance or time refund is owed, and the driver keeps the metered fare he earned on a 20.58 km, 26.8 minute trip.

The driver's explanation for the ERP line - 'The ERP is charged by the system' - is not a defence to a billing-integrity correction. POL-RD-09(4) makes the refund available whether or not a deviation exists, and the driver's counterparty statement points to no artifact showing the vehicle crossed the AYE Alexandra Rd gantry. The trace shows the vehicle's nearest fix 330.73 m away, so the system charged a gantry the trip did not cross. The driver's assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08 because it cites no evidence ID and no clause.

The driver's traffic-advisory route is closed on this record. The bundle holds a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY artifact, EV-ADVIS-02816-01, but its admissibility status is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload: no advisory covers the Tampines Mall corridor in this window. Under POL-RD-13 the driver's traffic assertion cannot be tested against any advisory, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The driver named no advisory evidence ID, so this is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged on this ground.

The driver's profile does not support any adverse finding and should not be used against him. His deviation_flags_90d is 0 and his completed_trips_90d is 395, so the POL-RD-06 pattern test (3 or more flags, or a ratio of 0.05 or more) is nowhere near met. His no_show_terminations_30d of 2 is a NO_SHOW_CHARGE field with no application to a route-deviation dispute, and his prior_no_show_flags and prior_deviation_flags are lifetime counters that POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting for the trailing-window figures. No repeat-deviation uplift or conduct referral is available on this record.

The rider's profile likewise carries no adverse finding. Her deviation_claims_60d is 1 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration trigger (4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) is not met and no extra corroboration is required of her claim. Her no_show_disputes_30d of 1 and her disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0 are the only other citable fields, and neither bears on this trip. Her prior_disputes_filed and prior_disputes_upheld are context only under POL-GEN-01.

The trace is clean for policy purposes and the rider's burden is discharged. The GPS artifact carries 162 fixes at a 10 s sample interval with 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0, so none of the POL-RD-07(a) to (c) impairment limbs fires. The trip identifiers on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown all read TRP-02816, and the pickup timestamp of 2026-08-30T10:49:30 matches across the trace and the trip record, satisfying POL-RD-08(a). The rider has therefore shown the artifacts describe the same trip and that the ERP line is unmatched, and the burden shifts to the driver, who has pointed to no artifact and no clause that excuses the charge.

The refund is small and the case should not be escalated. The contested amount is $3.00, the refund under POL-RD-09(4) is $3.00, and the recomputed fare under POL-RD-02 is $26.72 against a charged total of $30.55, a difference of $3.83 that is well below the SGD 150.00 escalation ceiling in POL-RD-10(6) and below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold in POL-GEN-05. The only unmatched charge line is the ERP line refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excludes from the escalation trigger. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires and the case can be decided on the money.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The rider disputed a $3.00 ERP charge for a road the trip never used. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02816) carries exactly one ERP line, 'AYE Alexandra Rd gantry', at $3.00, and the platform's own comparison of that gantry's coordinates (lat 1.289647, lng 103.863838) against the driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-02816) shows the closest the vehicle ever came was 330.73 m, at 11:10:50. POL-RD-09 treats a fix within 250 m of a gantry as a crossing; 330.73 m is outside that radius, so the trace never passes this gantry. Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge line for a gantry the trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure and is refunded in full as a standalone correction, whether or not a deviation exists. The $3.00 is therefore returned to the rider, and the case is recorded for billing-integrity review. This is a PARTIAL_REFUND: it returns the contested ERP line only, not the whole fare.

The driver's answer — 'the ERP is charged by the system' — is no defence to this correction. It names no gantry, road or evidence, carries no weight, and cannot show the vehicle crossed a gantry the trace places 330.73 m away.

The distance and time charges are left standing. On the trace the driven distance is 20.58 km against the 19.6 km optimal route — an excess of 0.98 km, or 5.00%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be both more than 20% of optimal and more than 0.8 km; the percentage test fails, so no deviation is established, no POL-RD-02 recomputation runs, and the driver keeps the metered distance and time charges for the 20.58 km, 26.8-minute trip.

No repeat-deviation or conduct finding arises. The driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 395 completed trips in 90 days, so no POL-RD-06 pattern is established and no POL-RD-06(c) referral issues; the lifetime counters prior_no_show_flags and prior_deviation_flags are context only under POL-GEN-01 and are not used. The rider's profile likewise bars nothing and demands no extra corroboration (1 claim in 60 days, 0 substantiated). The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes — 162 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gaps — trip identifiers match across the trip record, trace and fare breakdown (TRP-02816), and no POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires.

Figures used: charged_total $30.55 (EV-FARE-02816); ERP line $3.00; optimal distance 19.6 km and trace distance 20.58 km (EV-GPS-02816); nearest fix 330.73 m. The ruling rests on the fare breakdown and the GPS trace, both at full weight 1.0. Its monetary effect, $3.00, is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold (POL-GEN-05), so it executes on issue. Either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. This ruling concerns trip TRP-02816 (Tampines Mall to Blk 456 Hougang Ave 10, 30 Aug 2026), charged at a total of $30.55.

The ERP charge. The fare breakdown carries exactly one ERP line — AYE Alexandra Rd gantry, $3.00, charged 10:58:30 — and the optimal route's own ERP total is $0.00. Both the fare ledger and the platform's GPS analysis record that gantry as not on the optimal route. POL-RD-09 matches a gantry to the trip by treating any GPS fix within 250 m of it as a crossing. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes — 162 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0 seconds — so the match test can be run, and the closest the vehicle ever came to this gantry was 330.73 m (fix 128, 11:10:50). That is outside the 250 m radius, so the trace never passes the gantry and the line is a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4): the $3.00 is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not any deviation exists, and the matter is recorded for billing-integrity review. The $3.00 is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold in POL-GEN-05 (and no safety or complaint flag applies), so the refund executes on issue.

The distance and time charges. The rider does not assert, and I do not find, a route deviation. The trace measures 20.58 km against a booked optimal of 19.6 km — an excess of 0.98 km, or 5.00%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed both 20% of optimal and 0.8 km, and the percentage test fails, so no deviation is established and POL-RD-02 does not run. I have accordingly not used the $26.72 recomputed fare or the $3.83 difference between it and the $30.55 charged total: that difference is driven by this disputed ERP line and by distance and time the deviation rules do not reach. The driver keeps the metered distance and time charges. There is also no unbilled-distance compensation for the driver: the ledger bills 20.6 km against a 20.58 km trace, so POL-RD-04's shortfall limb is not met.

The parties' statements and profiles. The driver's counter-statement — 'The ERP is charged by the system' — cites no evidence ID, names no gantry, road or route, and points to no artifact showing the vehicle crossed the gantry. Under POL-RD-08 it carries no weight and does not discharge the driver's burden on this charge. The bundle's traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-02816-01) is MISSING with weight 0.0 and no payload, so no traffic explanation could have been tested against an advisory; because the driver named no advisory ID, that absence is a gap in the bundle and not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged and the case does not escalate on this ground. On the profiles: the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 395 completed trips in 90 days, and the rider's deviation_claims_60d is 1 with 0 substantiated, so neither the POL-RD-06 pattern test nor POL-RD-08's extra-corroboration trigger is met. Neither profile supports an adverse finding against either party, and the lifetime counters and other context-only fields (prior_deviation_flags, prior_no_show_flags, prior_disputes_filed, prior_disputes_upheld) were not used as grounds, as POL-GEN-01 requires. No conduct referral arises under POL-RD-06(c).

No escalation. Trip identifiers match across the trip record, GPS trace and fare breakdown; the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c); the timestamps are consistent; the refund is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling in POL-RD-10(6); and the only charge line without a trace or trip-record counterpart is the ERP line refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excludes. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires.

Outcome. PARTIAL_REFUND: $3.00 of the $5.00 contested is returned to the rider (the ERP pass-through correction), and the balance of the fare stands. The disputed amount is returned in part rather than in full, which is why the outcome is a partial refund rather than a full refund.

ledger.claim: The rider's claim is narrow and specific: a $3.00 ERP charge for a gantry on a road the trip never used. The fare ledger itself concedes the point — the single ERP line, 'AYE Alexandra Rd gantry' at $3.00, is flagged on_optimal_route = false, and the optimal route's own ERP total is $0.00. The rider was billed for a gantry that is not on the route they booked.

The driver's own GPS trace never comes within 250 m of the charged gantry. The nearest fix to the AYE Alexandra Rd gantry is 330.73 m away, at 11:10:50, and the trace does not bracket the gantry's closest approach. Under POL-RD-09 a gantry is matched to the trace by treating any fix within 250 m as a crossing; 330.73 m is outside that radius, so the trace does not place the vehicle at this gantry.

This is a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4): a charge line for a gantry the gps_trace never passes is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists. The $3.00 line should be refunded in full and the case recorded as a billing-integrity finding.

The rider's claim does not depend on establishing a route deviation, and I do not overreach by asserting one. The trace measures 20.58 km against an optimal of 19.6 km — an excess of 0.98 km, or 5.00%, which fails both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km). The derived deviation status is 'no deviation'. The rider's remedy therefore rests on the ERP pass-through correction alone, not on POL-RD-02.

The driver's counter-statement — 'The ERP is charged by the system' — cites no evidence ID and identifies no gantry, road or route. Under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded. It does not discharge the driver's burden of showing the charge was properly incurred.

No traffic advisory covers this trip window: the advisory artifact is MISSING with weight 0.0, so no external traffic cause can be tested or credited.
